'''Kyle Brandon O'Quinn''' (born March 26, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball|Norfolk State Spartans]], and led them to a victory over the #2 seed [[2011–12 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri Tigers]] in the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#West Regional – Phoenix, Arizona|second round]] of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. He was drafted in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] with the 49th overall pick, by the [[Orlando Magic]].

==Early and personal life==
O'Quinn was born in [[Queens, New York]], and grew up in [[South Jamaica, Queens]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6615/kyle-oquinn|title=Kyle O'Quinn - Philadelphia 76ers Center|website=ESPN}}</ref> His parents are Tommie (who moved to New York from Mississippi in 1963, worked for the [[Metropolitan Transportation Authority]], and died in a car accident in September 2015) and Regina O’Quinn.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2012/03/18/2012-ncaa-tournament-story-of-norfolk-state-and-kyle-oquinn-is-really-a-new-york-tale/|title=2012 NCAA Tournament: Story of Norfolk State and Kyle O'Quinn is really a New York tale|first=Mike|last=Lupica|website=[[New York Daily News]] |date=March 18, 2012}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated2>{{Cite web|url=https://www.msgnetworks.com/|title=Main|website=MSGNetworks.com}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/kyle/o'quinn/203124|title=Kyle O'Quinn | New York Knicks | NBA.com|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> He has an older sister, Rasheena Moss, who earned a degree in broadcast journalism from Hampton University in 2008.<ref name=autogenerated2 />

While playing for the Knicks, O'Quinn moonlighted by booking gigs in New York as a [[bar mitzvah]] and [[bat mitzvah]] entertainer; dancing with the teenagers, signing autographs, joining in [[selfie]]s with the kids, and chatting with the parents.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Ruth |title=Knicks' Kyle O'Quinn moonlights as a 'Bar Mitzvah Man' |url=https://nypost.com/2017/12/19/knicks-kyle-oquinn-moonlights-as-a-bar-mitzvah-man/ |access-date=25 August 2023 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=20 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Begley |first1=Ian |title=Kyle O'Quinn is a hit on the New York bar mitzvah scene |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21805972/nba-knicks-kyle-oquinn-hit-new-york-bar-mitzvah-scene |access-date=25 August 2023 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=19 December 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

==High school career==
O'Quinn first attended [[Holy Cross High School (Queens)|Holy Cross High School]] for his first two years of high school, playing only a limited amount on the school's junior varsity team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2012/06/26/norfolk-states-oquinn-serious-about-queens-to-nba-leap/|title=Norfolk State's O'Quinn serious about Queens-to-NBA leap|date=June 26, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://marshallreview.wordpress.com/2012/06/08/kyle-oquinn-is-closer-to-his-dreams/|title = Kyle O'Quinn is closer to his dreams| newspaper=The Marshall Review |date = June 8, 2012}}</ref> He then attended Math, Science Research & Technology High School at the [[Andrew Jackson High School (Queens)|Campus Magnet Complex]] in Queens, originally to play [[American football|football]], and almost quit basketball when he didn't play as a junior. In his senior year, he averaged 20 points, 12 rebounds, and 3 blocks per game, but his only scholarship offer was to [[Norfolk State University]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Lupica |first=Mike |title=Lupica: New York tale at the NCAA Tournament |url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2012-03-18/news/31205821_1_coach-eric-barnett-basketball-players-ncaa-tournament/2 |date=March 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711060116/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2012-03-18/news/31205821_1_coach-eric-barnett-basketball-players-ncaa-tournament/2 |archive-date=July 11, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a first-team All-Queens and third-team All-[[Public School Athletic League]] (PSAL) selection in his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nsuspartans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kyle-o-quinn/1339|title=Kyle O'Quinn - Men's Basketball|website=Norfolk State University Athletics}}</ref>

==College career==
O'Quinn originally planned on pursuing a career in [[American football|football]] even after receiving a scholarship from [[Norfolk State]] mainly because of his basketball ability. O'Quinn could have given up basketball the way he had with football, but this time chose the other choice and focused on pursuing a career in the [[NBA]]. He graduated with a degree in interdisciplinary studies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nbpa.com/norfolk-states-beloved-spartan-returns-inside-kyle-oquinns-graduation-weekend/|title=Norfolk State's Beloved Spartan Returns: Inside Kyle O'Quinn's Graduation Weekend - National Basketball Players Association<!-- Bot generated title -->|access-date=December 20, 2017|archive-date=December 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222051900/https://nbpa.com/norfolk-states-beloved-spartan-returns-inside-kyle-oquinns-graduation-weekend/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In his Norfolk State career, he played in 129 games, averaging 12.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.19 blocks, and shot .553 (610–1,104) from the field.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> Norfolk State Retired his number 10 jersey on February 16, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mitch|last=Brown|url=https://wtkr.com/2019/01/28/norfolk-state-set-to-retire-kyle-oquinns-basketball-jersey-in-february/|title=Norfolk State set to retire Kyle O'Quinn's basketball jersey in February|work=wtvr.com|date=January 28, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Hall|url=https://pilotonline.com/sports/college/norfolk-state/basketball/article_70f01024-3252-11e9-91d8-f79bb10d2a5b.html|title=As his NSU jersey is retired, Kyle O'Quinn shares the credit|work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]]|date=February 16, 2019|access-date=February 16, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Freshman season===
In O'Quinn's freshman season at Norfolk State (2008–09), he appeared in all 31 games including two starts. He averaged 5.3 points per game and 3.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He was also twice named the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference rookie of the week.

===Sophomore season===
In his sophomore season (2009–10), O'Quinn appeared in 30 games, starting in 29 of them. He was third on Norfolk State in scoring at 11.5 points per game, led the team in rebounds at 8.7 rebounds per game, and had 1.70 blocks per game. He also led the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] (MEAC) in field goal percentage at 54.9%.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> O'Quinn was also named to the All-MEAC Second Team and was twice named the MEAC Defensive Player of the Week.

===Junior season===
In O'Quinn's junior season in 2010–11, he averaged 16.4 points per game, 11.1 rebounds per game, and 3.44 blocks per game.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He was fourth in the country in blocked shots, fifth in rebounds, and eighth in double-doubles (19).<ref name=autogenerated1 /> O'Quinn led the MEAC in blocks and rebounds, was second in field goal percentage (.556), and finished fifth in points per game.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He established single-season school records ([[NCAA Division I]] era) with 110 blocked shots and 355 rebounds.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He also became the first-ever player from Norfolk State to be named MEAC Defensive Player of the Year. O'Quinn was named MEAC Defensive Player of the Week four times and was named MEAC Player of the Week four times as well, and was voted to the MEAC All-Tournament Team.<ref name=autogenerated1 />

===Senior season===
In O'Quinn's senior season, he averaged 15.9 points per game, 10.3 rebounds per game, and 2.69 blocks per game.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He led the conference and tied for fifth in the country with 20 double-doubles. He ranked 14th in the nation in field goal percentage (.573; 205–358), 15th in blocked shots, and 16th in rebounding.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He was named the MEAC Player of the Year and the MEAC Defensive Player of the Year.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He was the 2012 Lou Henson recipient as the nation's top mid-major player.<ref name=autogenerated1 />

Norfolk State made the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as a 15 seed, the Spartans (making their first-ever postseason appearance) upset the second-seeded [[Missouri Tigers]] in the Round of 64. In the game, O'Quinn recorded 26 points and 14 rebounds.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> After the game, an ecstatic O'Quinn began sprinting through the school's hallways, yelling, "We messed up some brackets! We messed up some brackets!" In the next round, Norfolk State lost to the [[Florida Gators]], and O'Quinn only recorded four points and three rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kyle O'Quinn Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kyle-oquinn-1.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=November 19, 2013}}</ref>

Following the season, O'Quinn participated in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], averaging 11.7 PPG, 11.7 RPG, and 3.7 BPG.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> O'Quinn was named the Tournament MVP, and was also named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norfolk State hero Kyle O'Quinn wins MVP at Portsmouth Invitational|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/04/15/norfolk-state-hero-kyle-oquinn-wins-mvp-at-portsmouth-invitational/|work=NBCSports.com|date=April 15, 2012|access-date=November 19, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Orlando Magic (2012–2015)===
O'Quinn was drafted in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] with the 49th overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2012/prospects/kyle-oquinn/ |title=PROSPECT PROFILE: KYLE O'QUINNyeee |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-11-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319073856/http://www.nba.com/draft/2012/prospects/kyle-oquinn/ |archive-date=2017-03-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 9, 2012, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Magic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-kyle-oquinn_080912|title=Magic Sign Kyle O'Quinn|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> He went on to earn the 2012–13 Hustle Player of the Year award for his constant commitment to playing every game with more excitement than the last.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/kyle-oquinn-earns-aleve-hustle-player-year-honors|title=Kyle O'Quinn Earns Aleve Hustle Player of the Year Honors|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> He finished the season with averages of 4.1 points and 3.7 rebounds in 57 games.

With 1.3 blocked shots per game in 2013–14, O'Quinn led the Magic and was tied for 20th in the league. He finished the season with averages of 6.2 points and 5.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oquinky01.html|title=Kyle O'Quinn Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

After spraining his ankle in the season opener against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on October 28, 2014, O'Quinn missed 15 consecutive games before returning to action on November 16. Over a five-game stretch with [[Nikola Vučević]] out with a back injury between December 2 and December 12, O'Quinn started all five games and subsequently averaged 15.4 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://orlandomagicdaily.com/2014/12/09/kyle-oquinns-starting-campaign/|title=Kyle O'Quinn's starting campaign}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oquinky01/gamelog/2015/|title=Kyle O'Quinn 2014-15 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2015–2018)===
[[File:Kyle O'Quinn (32600212586).jpg|thumb|O'Quinn with the Knicks in 2017.]]
On July 9, 2015, O'Quinn was signed-and-traded (to a four-year, $16-million contract)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-knicks-sign-kyle-o-quinn-queens-native-to-4-year-16m-deal-y31447|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707041624/http://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-knicks-sign-kyle-o-quinn-queens-native-to-4-year-16m-deal-1.10610209|url-status=live|archive-date=July 7, 2015|title=Sources: Kyle O'Quinn comes to hometown Knicks in four-year, $16M deal | Newsday<!-- Bot generated title -->}}</ref> from the Magic to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for cash considerations and the right to exchange 2019 second-round draft selections.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-four-free-agents-afflalo-r.-lopez-williams-oquinn|title=Knicks Acquire Four Free Agents: Afflalo, R. Lopez, Williams, O'Quinn|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 10, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Knicks, his hometown team, in the team's season opener against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on October 28, recording 8 points and 11 rebounds in a 122–97 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 24, Knicks beat Bucks 122-97 in opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026223709/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 26, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 24, 2016, he scored a season-high 19 points off the bench in a 108–105 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/NYKIND/gameinfo.html|title=George scores 25 of his 27 in 2nd half, Pacers edge Knicks|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160225100823/http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/NYKIND/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 25, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 2, 2016, O'Quinn recorded season highs of 20 points and 13 rebounds in a 118–114 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899727|title=Anthony scores 29, Knicks defeat Timberwolves 118-114|work=ESPN.com|date=December 2, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> On December 22, he recorded 14 points and a career-high 16 rebounds in a 106–95 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899880|title=Rose leads 6 Knicks in double figures, Knicks beat Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2016|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> On March 16, 2017, he came off the bench to a tie a career high with 23 points in a 121–110 loss to the Brooklyn Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900411|title=Nets beat Knicks again, get 121-110 win at MSG|work=ESPN.com|date=March 16, 2017|access-date=March 17, 2017}}</ref>

On November 25, 2017, O'Quinn had his first double-double of the season with 20 points and 15 rebounds starting in place of the injured [[Enes Kanter]] in a 117–102 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975033|title=Harden leads Rockets to 117-102 win over Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 25, 2017|access-date=November 25, 2017}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2018–2019)===
On July 9, 2018, O'Quinn signed a one-year deal with the [[Indiana Pacers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-kyle-oquinn|title=Pacers Sign Kyle O'Quinn|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}}</ref> after opting out of the final year of his contract in New York. His decision landed him $4.5 million, a $200,000 raise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070786|title=Sabonis, Oladipo lift Pacers over Knicks 107-101|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2018|access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2020)===
On July 11, 2019, O’Quinn signed a one-year deal with [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Team Signs O'Quinn|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-oquinn|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2019|date=July 11, 2019}}</ref>

===Fenerbahçe (2021)===
On January 20, 2021, O'Quinn signed a one-year deal with [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kyle O'Quinn Fenerbahçe Beko'da |url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2021/1/kyle-o-quinn-fenerbahce-beko-da |website=fenerbahce.org |access-date=January 20, 2021 |language=tr-TR |date=January 20, 2021}}</ref> On June 17, 2021, O'Quinn officially parted ways with the Turkish club.

===Paris Basketball (2021–2022)===
On September 2, 2021, O'Quinn signed with [[Paris Basketball]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kyle-oquinn-officially-signs-with-paris-basketball/|title=Kyle O'Quinn officially signs with Paris Basketball|last=|first=|date=September 2, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Sichuan Blue Whales (2023)===
On September 24, 2023, O'Quinn signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kyle O'Quinn signs with Sichuan Blue Whales |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kyle-oquinn-signs-with-sichuan-blue-whales/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 26, 2023 |date=September 24, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

On April 12, 2025, O'Quinn announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Dimmitt|title=Former NBA center announces retirement|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/former_nba_center_announces_retirement/s1_14822_42040218|website=yardbarker.com|date=April 12, 2025|access-date=April 13, 2025}}</ref>
